target.title: fix(agents): decouple MCP retirement from browser cleanup
target.body:
Related: #76233
Related: #101830

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a completed run-mode subagent waits for sequential browser-tab cleanup before retiring its bundle MCP runtime and starting completion delivery. A browser close request can wait up to the browser service timeout per tab, so one run with several tabs can delay MCP retirement, the completion announcement, and the next same-session turn.

The concrete sequential browser-cleanup delay is separate from the MCP lease-disposal race covered by #76233 and the related #101830 work.

## Why This Change Was Made

Browser cleanup is dispatched as independent owner-scoped work, while MCP retirement and completion announcement proceed after the existing generation and lease-safety checks. Browser operations hold a per-session access gate for their full request; cleanup takes the exclusive gate, so a successor browser turn waits safely instead of racing an already-issued close request.

The browser registry tracks the opaque run owner and an ordered ownership claim. Successor reuse transfers ownership; late predecessor callbacks cannot reclaim or remove the successor tab. Failed non-ignorable closes remain tracked for a later cleanup, and legacy unowned tabs remain eligible for cleanup.

`runId` remains an additive, optional Plugin SDK context field. It is host-issued, stable for the active run, opaque, and absent outside an active run. Plugins may use it only to key ephemeral plugin-owned resources and cleanup; they must not parse it, persist it as application data, expose it to users, or use it as an authentication or authorization boundary. The contract is documented in `docs/plugins/building-plugins.md` and covered at the `defineToolPlugin` factory boundary in `src/plugin-sdk/tool-plugin.test.ts`; the existing agent-context test covers runtime propagation.

## User Impact

Run-mode subagent completion no longer waits for the browser service to close every tracked tab before MCP retirement and completion delivery begin. A successor turn can start its non-browser work immediately and its browser work is admitted after the old cleanup gate releases, preserving tab safety. App-view MCP leases continue to defer retirement until their release path completes.

## Evidence

Branch-attributable CI repair:

- `check-test-types` previously failed at `src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts(345,18)` because the successor fixture read optional `entry.startedAt`. The fixture now uses deterministic timestamps (`1_001`), and `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile /tmp/openclaw-core-test.tsbuildinfo` exits 0.
- The previous `checks-node-compact-large-1` failure is `ui/src/pages/chat/chat-responsive.browser.test.ts`, which is unchanged by this branch. The same file failed in current-main run [29217990227](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29217990227/job/86717742399) at a separate assertion.
- The previous `checks-node-compact-small-2` failure is `test/scripts/apple-app-i18n.test.ts`, caused by the unchanged `apps/ios/Sources/Design/SettingsProTabSections.swift`. Running that exact test in a disposable checkout of the PR base (`2f756c70a65ca345df10618b2900809936012028`) reproduced the same 2 failed / 11 passed result. No UI or iOS file is changed here.

Focused branch validation:

- `src/agents/subagent-registry-lifecycle.test.ts`: 88/88 passed.
- `src/plugin-sdk/tool-plugin.test.ts`: 6/6 passed.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.plugin-context.test.ts`: 20/20 passed.
- `extensions/browser/src/browser/session-tab-registry.test.ts`: 13/13 passed.
- `extensions/browser/src/browser-tool.test.ts`: 91/91 passed.
- `src/browser-lifecycle-cleanup.test.ts`: 4/4 passed.
- `oxfmt --check`, targeted `run-oxlint.mjs`, docs formatting, and `git diff --check` passed. Fresh Codex autoreview reported no accepted/actionable findings.
- `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs --check` reports the same pre-existing budget failure on base and branch (`public deprecated exports 3284 > 3279`, `conversation-runtime 4 > 0`, `channel-pairing 1 > 0`); this change does not alter the inventory.

Redacted runtime fallback evidence (local in-process runtime, no secrets or transcript):

```text
[runtime-proof/lifecycle] {"provider":"local-runtime-fallback","run":"old","session":"agent:…:child","events":["browser-cleanup-blocked","mcp-retirement-started","completion-announcement-started","completion-returned-before-browser-release","browser-cleanup-released"]}
[runtime-proof/browser] {"provider":"local-runtime-fallback","session":"agent:…:child","events":["browser-close-blocked","browser-close-released","successor-browser-access-resumed"]}
```

These are complementary deterministic barriers through the actual lifecycle controller and browser session registry, with the close/announce seams blocked inside the tests. The first proves completion proceeds before browser release; the second proves successor browser access resumes only after the exclusive cleanup gate releases. Identifiers are redacted. A browser-capable remote lease was not retained because the available DigitalOcean provider is SSH-only and its bootstrap was slower than the local fallback; AWS and Hetzner browser lanes were unavailable in this environment. The DigitalOcean attempt used provider `digitalocean`, lease `cbx_16823554cf26`, and was aborted before any runtime command; authenticated lease listing was empty afterward.

The remaining proof gap is a remote user-path run with a real browser service and captured completion/successor-turn timestamps. The source-level barriers and focused regression tests are present, but this environment could not produce that remote artifact without a slower or unavailable provider.

AI-assisted disclosure: This PR was implemented with Codex assistance. The author reviewed the source paths, dependency contracts, tests, and final diff, and verified the behavior described above. No transcript is included by request.

Allow edits from maintainers is enabled for this fork PR.
